section.content: The invention provides a machine learning device, which can restrain the situation that the amount of power which can be supplied from a vehicle to the outside in disaster is reduced by the processing related to the learning of a machine learning model in the vehicle which can supply power to the outside. The machine learning device is provided in a vehicle (3) capable of supplying electric power to the outside, and is provided with a learning unit (51) that performs processing relating to learning of a machine learning model used in the vehicle. When disaster information is acquired, the learning unit reduces the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process, as compared with the case where disaster information is not acquired.
本发明提供一种机器学习装置，在能够向外部供给电力的车辆中，抑制在灾害时能够从车辆向外部供给的电力量因与机器学习模型的学习相关的处理而减少的情况。机器学习装置设置于能够向外部供给电力的车辆(3)，并具备实施与在车辆中使用的机器学习模型的学习相关的处理的学习部(51)。学习部在取得了灾害信息的情况下，与未取得灾害信息的情况相比，使与学习相关的处理中的电力消耗量降低。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device.

Background

In recent years, with the development of AI (artificial intelligence) technology, control using a machine learning model such as a neural network model is being studied in a vehicle. For example, in the machine learning device described in patent document 1, learning of the neural network model is performed by an electronic control unit provided in the vehicle, and an estimated value of the temperature of the exhaust gas purifying catalyst is output from the learned neural network model.

Prior art literature

Patent literature

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open No. 2019-183698

Disclosure of Invention

Problems to be solved by the invention

However, in a vehicle having a large battery capacity such as a plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHV), the electric power stored in the battery can be supplied to the outside of the vehicle. Therefore, when a power failure occurs due to a disaster, the vehicle can be effectively used as a power supply source.

However, when processing related to learning of the machine learning model is performed in the vehicle, electric power required for learning is consumed in addition to electric power required for running of the vehicle. As a result, the power consumption in the vehicle increases, and the power required at the time of the disaster may not be ensured.

In view of the above-described problems, an object of the present invention is to prevent, in a vehicle capable of supplying electric power to the outside, an amount of electric power that can be supplied from the vehicle to the outside at the time of a disaster from being reduced by a process related to learning of a machine learning model.

Means for solving the problems

The gist of the present disclosure is as follows.

(1) The machine learning device is provided in a vehicle capable of supplying electric power to the outside, and is provided with a learning unit that performs processing related to learning of a machine learning model used in the vehicle, wherein the learning unit reduces the amount of electric power consumption in the processing related to learning when disaster information is acquired, as compared with when the disaster information is not acquired.

(2) The machine learning device according to the above (1), wherein the machine learning device further includes a position information acquisition unit that acquires position information of the vehicle, and when power supply from the vehicle to the outside is predicted based on the disaster information and the position information, the learning unit reduces the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process, compared to a case where the power supply is not predicted.

(3) The machine learning device according to the above (2), wherein the position information acquisition unit acquires a destination of the vehicle, and the learning unit reduces the power consumption amount when the supply of power from the vehicle to the outside is predicted based on the disaster information and the destination, as compared with a case where the supply of power is not predicted.

(4) The machine learning device according to any one of the above (1) to (3), wherein the learning section reduces the electric power consumption amount by stopping the process related to the learning.

(5) The machine learning device according to the above (4), wherein the machine learning device further includes an output device control unit that controls an output device provided to the vehicle, the output device control unit confirms to a driver of the vehicle via the output device permission to stop the learning-related process, and the learning unit does not stop the learning-related process when the driver does not permit stopping the learning-related process.

(6) A machine learning device is provided with: a communication device capable of communicating with a vehicle capable of supplying electric power to the outside; and a control device that performs learning of the machine learning model and transmits the learned machine learning model to the vehicle via the communication device, wherein the control device stops transmission of the learned machine learning model to the vehicle when disaster information is acquired.

Effects of the invention

According to the present invention, in a vehicle capable of supplying electric power to the outside, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the amount of electric power that can be supplied from the vehicle to the outside at the time of a disaster, due to processing related to learning of a machine learning model.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings. In the following description, the same reference numerals are given to the same constituent elements.

< First embodiment >, first embodiment

First, a first embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to fig. 1 to 6. Fig. 1 is a schematic configuration diagram of a machine learning system 1 according to a first embodiment of the present invention. The machine learning system 1 includes a server 2 and a vehicle 3.

As shown in fig. 1, the server 2 is provided outside the vehicle 3, and includes a communication interface 21, a storage device 22, a memory 23, and a processor 24. The server 2 may further include an input device such as a keyboard and a mouse, an output device such as a display, and the like. The server 2 may be constituted by a plurality of computers.

The communication interface 21 is capable of communicating with the vehicle 3, and enables the server 2 to communicate with the vehicle 3. Specifically, the communication interface 21 has an interface circuit for connecting the server 2 to the communication network 5. The server 2 communicates with the vehicle 3 via the communication interface 21, the communication network 5, and the wireless base station 6. The communication interface 21 is an example of a communication device.

The storage device 22 has, for example, a Hard Disk Drive (HDD), a Solid State Drive (SSD), or an optical recording medium. The storage device 22 stores various data, such as information related to the vehicle 3, a computer program for causing the processor 24 to execute various processes, and the like.

The memory 23 has a semiconductor memory such as a Random Access Memory (RAM). The memory 23 stores various data and the like, for example, used when various processes are executed by the processor 24.

The communication interface 21, the storage device 22, and the memory 23 are connected to the processor 24 via signal lines. The processor 24 has one or more CPUs and peripheral circuits thereof, and performs various processes. The processor 24 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logic arithmetic unit or a numerical arithmetic unit. The processor 24 is an example of a control device.

Fig. 2 is a diagram schematically showing a configuration of a vehicle 3 provided with a machine learning device according to a first embodiment of the present invention. The vehicle 3 is a vehicle that can supply electric power to the outside of the vehicle 3, and is, for example, a plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHV), an Electric Vehicle (EV), a Fuel Cell Vehicle (FCV), or the like.

As shown in fig. 2, the vehicle 3 includes a Human-machine interface (Human MACHINE INTERFACE (HMI)) 31, a GPS receiver 32, a map database 33, a navigation system 34, an actuator 35, a sensor 36, a communication module 37, and an electronic control unit (ECU (Electronic Control Unit)) 40. The HMI31, the GPS receiver 32, the map database 33, the navigation system 34, the actuator 35, the sensor 36, and the communication module 37 are communicably connected to the ECU40 via an in-vehicle network conforming to the standard such as CAN (Controller Area Network: controller area network).

The HMI31 is an input/output device that inputs/outputs information between the driver and the vehicle 3. The HMI31 includes, for example, a display that displays information, a speaker that generates sound, an operation button or touch screen for input operation by the driver, a microphone that receives the sound of the driver, and the like. The output of the ECU40 is transmitted to the driver via the HMI31, and the input from the driver is transmitted to the ECU40 via the HMI 31.

The GPS receiver 32 receives signals from three or more GPS satellites and detects the current position of the vehicle 3 (for example, the latitude and longitude of the vehicle 3). The output of the GPS receiver 32 is sent to the ECU40.

The map database 33 stores map information. The ECU40 acquires map information from the map database 33.

The navigation system 34 sets a travel route to the vehicle at the destination based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 32, map information of the map database 33, an input made by the driver of the vehicle, and the like. The travel route set by the navigation system 34 is sent to the ECU40. In addition, the GPS receiver 32 and the map database 33 may also be combined with the navigation system 34.

The actuator 35 is a working member required for running of the vehicle 3. In the case where the vehicle 3 is PHV, the actuator 35 includes, for example, an electric motor, a fuel injection valve, a spark plug, a throttle valve drive actuator, an EGR control valve, and the like. The ECU40 controls the actuator 35.

The sensors 36 detect state quantities of the vehicle 3, the internal combustion engine, the battery, and the like, including a vehicle speed sensor, an accelerator opening sensor, an air flow meter, an air-fuel ratio sensor, a crank angle sensor, a torque sensor, a voltage sensor, and the like. The output of the sensor 36 is sent to the ECU40.

The communication module 37 is a device capable of communicating the vehicle 3 with the outside of the vehicle 3. The communication module 37 is, for example, a data communication module (DCM (Data communication module)) capable of communicating with the communication network 5 via the radio base station 6. In addition, as the communication module 37, a mobile terminal (for example, a smart phone, a tablet terminal, a WiFi router, or the like) may also be used.

The ECU40 includes a communication interface 41, a memory 42, and a processor 43, and executes various controls of the vehicle 3. In the present embodiment, one ECU40 is provided, but a plurality of ECUs may be provided for each function.

The communication interface 41 has an interface circuit for connecting the ECU40 to an in-vehicle network conforming to the CAN or the like. The ECU40 communicates with other in-vehicle devices as described above via the communication interface 41.

The memory 42 has, for example, a volatile semiconductor memory (e.g., RAM) and a nonvolatile semiconductor memory (e.g., ROM). The memory 42 stores programs executed in the processor 43, various data used when various processes are executed by the processor 43, and the like.

The processor 43 has one or more CPUs (Central Processing Unit: central processing unit) and peripheral circuits thereof, and performs various processes. The processor 43 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logic arithmetic unit or a numerical arithmetic unit. The communication interface 41, the memory 42, and the processor 43 are connected to each other via signal lines.

In the present embodiment, the ECU40 functions as a machine learning device. Fig. 3 is a functional block diagram of the ECU40 in the first embodiment. The ECU40 has a learning unit 51. The learning unit 51 is a functional block realized by causing the processor 43 of the ECU40 to execute a program stored in the memory 42 of the ECU 40.

The learning unit 51 performs processing related to learning of the machine learning model used in the vehicle 3. In the present embodiment, the learning unit 51 performs processing related to learning of the neural network model using the neural network model as the machine learning model. First, an outline of the neural network model will be described with reference to fig. 4. Fig. 4 shows an example of a neural network model having a simple structure.

The circle marks in fig. 4 represent artificial neurons. Artificial neurons are commonly referred to as nodes or units (in this specification, referred to as "nodes"). In fig. 4, l=1 represents an input layer, l=2 and l=3 represents a hidden layer, and l=4 represents an output layer. In addition, the hidden layer is also referred to as an intermediate layer.

In fig. 4, x 1 and x 2 denote each node of the input layer (l=1) and an output value from the node, and y denotes a node of the output layer (l=4) and an output value thereof. Similarly, z 1(L＝2)、z2(L＝2) and z 3(L＝2) denote each node of the hidden layer (l=2) and an output value from the node, and z 1(L＝3) and z 2(L＝3) denote each node of the hidden layer (l=3) and an output value from the node.

At each node of the input layer, the input is directly output. On the other hand, the output values x 1 and x 2 of the respective nodes of the input layer are input to the respective nodes of the hidden layer (l=2), and the total input value u is calculated at the respective nodes of the hidden layer (l=2) using the weights w and the deviations b, respectively. For example, the total input value u k(L＝2) calculated at each node, represented by z k(L＝2) (k=1, 2, 3) of the hidden layer (l=2) in fig. 4, is shown as follows (M is the number of nodes of the input layer).

[ Math 1]

Then, the total input value u k(L＝2) is converted by the activation function f, and is output from a node indicated by z k(L＝2) of the hidden layer (l=2) as an output value z k(L＝2)(＝f(uk(L＝2)). On the other hand, the output values z 1(L＝2)、z2(L＝2) and z 3(L＝2) of each node of the hidden layer (l=2) are input to each node of the hidden layer (l=3), and the total input value u (= Σz·w+b) is calculated using the weight w and the deviation b corresponding to each node of the hidden layer (l=3). The total input value u is similarly converted by an activation function, for example, a Sigmoid function σ, and output as an output value z 1(L＝3)、z2(L＝3) from each node of the hidden layer (l=3).

The output values z 1(L＝3) and z 2(L＝3) of the respective nodes of the hidden layer (l=3) are input to the node of the output layer (l=4), and the total input value u (Σz·w+b) is calculated using the weight w and the deviation b corresponding to each node of the output layer, or the total input value u (Σz·w) is calculated using only the weight w corresponding to each node. For example, at a node of the output layer, an identity function is used as the activation function. In this case, the total input value u calculated at the node of the output layer is directly output from the node of the output layer as the output value y.

The neural network model used in the vehicle 3 is stored in the memory 42 of the ECU40 or other storage device provided in the vehicle 3. The ECU40 causes the neural network model to output at least one output parameter by inputting a plurality of input parameters to the neural network model. At this time, as the value of each input parameter, for example, a value detected by the sensor 36 or the like or a value calculated in the ECU40 is used. By using the neural network model, a value of an appropriate output parameter corresponding to an input parameter of a prescribed value can be obtained.

In order to improve the accuracy of such a neural network model, it is necessary to learn the neural network model in advance. In the present embodiment, the ECU40 of the vehicle 3 performs learning of the neural network model. That is, the learning of the neural network model is performed not in the server 2 but in the vehicle 3.

In learning the neural network model, a training data set composed of a combination of actual measurement values of a plurality of input parameters and actual measurement values (correct answer data) of at least one output parameter corresponding to the actual measurement values is used. Therefore, as a process related to learning of the neural network model (hereinafter referred to as "learning related process"), the learning section 51 of the ECU40 performs creation of a training data set. Specifically, the learning unit 51 obtains actual measurement values of a plurality of input parameters and actual measurement values of at least one output parameter corresponding to the actual measurement values, and creates a training data set by combining the actual measurement values of the input parameters and the actual measurement values of the output parameters.

The actual measurement value of the input parameter and the actual measurement value of the output parameter are obtained, for example, as values detected by the sensor 36 or the like or values calculated or determined by the ECU 40. The training data set created by the learning section 51 is stored in the memory 42 of the ECU40 or other storage device provided in the vehicle 3. In addition, the actual measurement value of the input parameter used as the training data set may be normalized or standardized.

Further, as learning-related processing, the learning unit 51 performs learning of the neural network model. Specifically, the learning unit 51 repeatedly updates the weights w and the deviations b in the neural network model by a known error back propagation algorithm using a large number of training data sets so that the difference between the output value of the neural network model and the actual measured value of the output parameter becomes small. As a result, the neural network model is learned, and a learned neural network model is generated. The information (model structure, weight w, deviation b, etc.) of the neural network model after learning is stored in the memory 42 of the ECU40 or in another storage device provided in the vehicle 3. By using the neural network model learned in the vehicle 3, the value of the output parameter corresponding to the input parameter of the predetermined value can be predicted without detecting the value of the actual output parameter by the sensor 36 or the like.

However, as described above, in the vehicle 3, the electric power stored in the battery of the vehicle 3 can be supplied to the outside of the vehicle 3. Therefore, when a power failure occurs due to a disaster, the vehicle 3 can be effectively utilized as a power supply source.

However, when the learning-related process is performed in the vehicle 3, the electric power required for learning is consumed in addition to the electric power required for running of the vehicle 3. As a result, the power consumption amount in the vehicle 3 increases, and the power required at the time of the disaster may not be ensured.

Therefore, in the present embodiment, when disaster information is acquired, the learning unit 51 reduces the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process as compared with the case where disaster information is not acquired. This can suppress a decrease in the amount of electric power that can be supplied from the vehicle 3 to the outside at the time of a disaster due to the learning-related process.

The disaster information includes information (location information of disaster-affected areas, etc.) related to natural disasters (earthquakes, typhoons, volcanic fires, floods, etc.) and artificial disasters (blackouts, etc. caused by work errors). For example, the learning unit 51 receives disaster information from outside the vehicle 3 to acquire the disaster information. In this case, the server 2 receives disaster information from public institutions (weather bureau, national transportation province, etc.), electric power companies, etc., and transmits the disaster information to the vehicle 3.

On the other hand, the learning unit 51 of the ECU40 stops the learning-related process when disaster information is received from the server 2. That is, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process to reduce the power consumption amount (set to zero) in the learning-related process.

The above control will be described below with reference to flowcharts of fig. 5 and 6. Fig. 5 is a flowchart showing a control routine of disaster information transmission processing in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 24 of the server 2 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S101, the processor 24 determines whether disaster information is received. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S102.

In step S102, the processor 24 transmits disaster information to the vehicle 3. After step S102, the present control routine ends.

In addition, disaster information may be input to the server 2 by an operator of the server 2 or the like, and the processor 24 may determine whether or not disaster information is input to the server 2 in step S101.

Fig. 6 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning stop process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU40 of the vehicle 3 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S201, the learning unit 51 determines whether disaster information is received from the server 2. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received from the server 2, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information has been received from the server 2, the present control routine proceeds to step S202.

In step S202, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process. Specifically, the learning unit 51 stops creation of the training data set and learning of the neural network model. At this time, the driver may be notified of the stop of the learning-related process to suppress the power consumption by text or sound via the HMI 31. After step S202, the present control routine ends. In this case, the learning unit 51 resumes the learning-related process when, for example, a predetermined time elapses, the vehicle 3 restarts, the driver of the vehicle 3 instructs the resumption of the learning-related process via the HMI31, or the server 2 notifies the elimination of the disaster.

Further, since the power consumption amount for learning the neural network model is the largest in the learning-related process, the learning unit 51 may stop learning only the neural network model in step S202.

The learning unit 51 may reduce the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process without stopping the learning-related process. In this case, the learning unit 51 reduces the power consumption by, for example, reducing the frequency of creation of the training data set, reducing the frequency of learning the neural network model, or slowing down the learning speed of the neural network model.

The learning unit 51 may directly receive disaster information from public institutions (weather bureau, national transportation province, etc.), electric power companies, and the like, without going through the server 2. The learning unit 51 may receive disaster information from another vehicle through inter-vehicle communication or acquire disaster information from a roadside apparatus through road-to-vehicle communication using the communication module 37. In these cases, the control routine of fig. 5 is omitted, and in step S201, the learning unit 51 determines whether disaster information is received.

< Second embodiment >

The structure and control of the machine learning device of the second embodiment are basically the same as those of the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a second embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly in a part different from the first embodiment.

Fig. 7 is a diagram schematically showing a configuration of a vehicle 3' provided with a machine learning device according to a second embodiment of the present invention. As shown in fig. 7, the vehicle 3' further includes an off-vehicle camera 38. The vehicle exterior camera 38 photographs the surroundings of the vehicle 3 'to generate an image of the surroundings of the vehicle 3'. For example, the vehicle exterior camera 38 is disposed in front of the vehicle 3 '(for example, the back surface of a mirror inside the vehicle, a front bumper, or the like) to capture images of the front of the vehicle 3'. The off-vehicle camera 38 may be a stereo camera capable of ranging.

In the second embodiment, the vehicle 3' detects a disaster. That is, the learning unit 51 of the ECU40 acquires disaster information by detecting a disaster. For example, the learning unit 51 determines whether or not there is a disaster around the vehicle 3' based on the surrounding image generated by the outside camera 38. Specifically, the learning unit 51 analyzes the peripheral image by using an image recognition technique such as machine learning (neural network, support vector machine, etc.), and thereby determines whether or not a disaster is present. For example, the learning unit 51 determines that a disaster has occurred around the vehicle 3' when a power failure of the traffic light, collapse of the building, cracks in the road surface, fallen trees, flooding of the road, landslide, or the like is recognized from the surrounding image. The sensor 36 includes a gyro sensor or the like, and the learning unit 51 may detect a disaster by detecting an earthquake by the sensor 36.

Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning stop process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU40 of the vehicle 3' at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S301, the learning unit 51 determines whether or not a disaster around the vehicle 3' is detected. When it is determined that a disaster has not been detected, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that a disaster has been detected, the present control routine advances to step S302.

In step S302, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process as in step S202 of fig. 6. After step S302, the present control routine ends. In this case, the learning unit 51 restarts the learning-related process, for example, when a predetermined time elapses, the vehicle 3 'restarts, or when the driver of the vehicle 3' instructs the restart of the learning-related process via the HMI 31. In addition, the control routine of fig. 8 may be modified in the same manner as the control routine of fig. 6.

< Third embodiment >

The structure and control of the machine learning device of the third embodiment are basically the same as those of the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a third embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly in a part different from the first embodiment.

Fig. 9 is a functional block diagram of the ECU40 in the third embodiment. In the third embodiment, the ECU40 includes a position information acquisition unit 52 in addition to the learning unit 51. The learning unit 51 and the positional information acquiring unit 52 are functional blocks realized by the processor 43 of the ECU40 executing programs stored in the memory 42 of the ECU 40.

The position information acquisition unit 52 acquires position information of the vehicle 3. For example, the position information acquisition unit 52 acquires the current position of the vehicle 3 based on the output of the GPS receiver 32. The position information of the vehicle 3 is periodically transmitted from the vehicle 3 to the server 2 together with the identification information (e.g., identification number) of the vehicle 3, and stored in the storage device 22 of the server 2.

However, even if a disaster occurs, when the vehicle 3 travels at a location far from the disaster-stricken area, the necessity of using the power supply of the vehicle 3 is low. Therefore, in the third embodiment, when the supply of electric power from the vehicle 3 to the outside is predicted based on the disaster information and the position information of the vehicle 3, the learning unit 51 reduces the amount of electric power consumption in the learning-related process, as compared with the case where the supply of electric power is not predicted. This can reduce the amount of power consumption consumed by the learning-related process at a more appropriate timing to prepare for power supply at the time of a disaster.

For example, the server 2 receives disaster information from public institutions (weather bureau, national transportation province, etc.), electric power companies, etc., and determines a disaster-stricken area predicted to be supplied with electric power from the vehicle to the outside. The position information of a plurality of vehicles in motion is periodically transmitted to the server 2, and the server 2 identifies vehicles in the disaster area by collating the position information of the vehicles and the disaster area.

In disaster areas, it is predicted that power is supplied from the vehicle to the outside in order to cope with power failure or the like. Therefore, the server 2 transmits a stop instruction of the learning-related process to the vehicle in the disaster area. The learning unit 51 of the ECU40 stops the learning-related process when receiving a stop instruction of the learning-related process from the server 2. That is, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process to reduce the power consumption amount (set to zero) in the learning-related process.

The above control will be described below with reference to flowcharts of fig. 10 and 11. Fig. 10 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the vehicle determination process in the third embodiment of the invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 24 of the server 2 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S401, the processor 24 determines whether disaster information is received. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S402.

In step S402, the processor 24 determines a vehicle in the disaster area by comparing the position information of the disaster area included in the disaster information with the position information of the vehicle (the current position of the vehicle) stored for each vehicle.

Next, in step S403, the processor 24 transmits a stop instruction of the learning-related process to the vehicle determined in step S402. After step S403, the present control routine ends.

In addition, disaster information may be input to the server 2 by an operator of the server 2 or the like, and the processor 24 may determine whether or not disaster information is input to the server 2 in step S401.

Fig. 11 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning stop process in the third embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU40 of the vehicle 3 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S501, the learning unit 51 determines whether or not a stop instruction of the learning-related process is received from the server 2. If it is determined that the instruction to stop the learning-related process is not received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the instruction to stop the learning-related process is received, the present control routine advances to step S502.

In step S502, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process as in step S202 of fig. 6. After step S502, the present control routine ends. In this case, the learning unit 51 restarts the learning-related process, for example, when a predetermined time elapses, when the vehicle 3 restarts, when the driver of the vehicle 3 instructs the restart of the learning-related process via the HMI31, or when the server 2 instructs the restart of the learning-related process.

Further, since the power consumption amount for learning the neural network model is the largest in the learning-related process, the learning unit 51 may stop learning only the neural network model in step S502.

The processor 24 of the server 2 may transmit a power suppression instruction to the vehicle in the disaster area instead of the learning stop instruction. In this case, the learning unit 51 reduces the power consumption amount in the learning-related process without stopping the learning-related process when receiving the power suppression instruction from the server 2. For example, the learning unit 51 reduces the frequency of creation of the training data set, reduces the frequency of learning the neural network model, or slows down the learning speed of the neural network model.

< Fourth embodiment >

The structure and control of the machine learning device of the fourth embodiment are basically the same as those of the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a fourth embodiment of the present invention will be described below focusing on a portion different from the first embodiment.

In the fourth embodiment, disaster information is transmitted to the vehicle 3 instead of the server 2, and the learning unit 51 of the ECU40 acquires the disaster information. That is, the learning unit 51 receives disaster information from public institutions (weather bureau, national transportation province, etc.), electric power companies, etc., and determines a disaster-stricken area predicted to be supplied with electric power from the vehicle to the outside. The learning unit 51 may receive disaster information from another vehicle through inter-vehicle communication or acquire disaster information from a roadside apparatus through road-to-vehicle communication using the communication module 37.

When the vehicle 3 is located in the disaster area, the learning unit 51 reduces the power consumption amount in the learning-related process. Specifically, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process when the vehicle 3 is located in the disaster area.

Fig. 12 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning stop process in the fourth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU40 of the vehicle 3 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S601, the learning unit 51 determines whether disaster information is received. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received, the present control routine advances to step S602.

Next, in step S602, the learning unit 51 determines whether or not the vehicle 3 is located in the disaster area based on the disaster area location information included in the disaster information and the current location of the vehicle 3 acquired by the location information acquiring unit 52. If it is determined that the vehicle 3 is not located in the disaster area, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the vehicle 3 is located in the disaster area, the present control routine proceeds to step S603.

In step S603, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process as in step S202 of fig. 6. After step S603, the present control routine ends. In this case, the learning unit 51 restarts the learning-related process, for example, when a predetermined time elapses, the vehicle 3 restarts, or when the driver of the vehicle 3 instructs the restart of the learning-related process via the HMI 31.

Further, since the power consumption amount for learning the neural network model is the largest in the learning-related process, the learning unit 51 may stop learning only the neural network model in step S603.

In step S603, the learning unit 51 may reduce the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process without stopping the learning-related process. In this case, the learning unit 51 reduces the frequency of creating the training data set, reduces the frequency of learning the neural network model, or slows down the learning speed of the neural network model, for example.

< Fifth embodiment >

The structure and control of the machine learning device of the fifth embodiment are basically the same as those of the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a fifth embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly in a part different from the first embodiment.

Fig. 13 is a functional block diagram of the ECU40 in the fifth embodiment. The ECU40 includes an output device control unit 53 in addition to the learning unit 51 and the positional information acquisition unit 52. The learning unit 51, the positional information acquisition unit 52, and the output device control unit 53 are functional blocks realized by the processor 43 of the ECU40 executing programs stored in the memory 42 of the ECU 40.

The output device control unit 53 controls an output device provided in the vehicle 3. In the present embodiment, the output device control unit 53 controls the HMI 31. The HMI31 is an example of an output device.

As described above, the learning unit 51 reduces the power consumption amount in the learning-related process at the time of a disaster, and supplies power to the outside of the vehicle 3. However, in disaster areas, power failure does not necessarily occur. In addition, the driver may not want to supply electric power from the vehicle 3 to the outside at the time of disaster.

Accordingly, the output device control section 53 confirms the permission to stop the learning-related process to the driver of the vehicle 3 via the HMI 31. The learning unit 51 can stop the learning-related process when the driver is permitted to stop the learning-related process, and can stop the learning-related process in preparation for the power supply at the time of the disaster based on the intention of the driver without stopping the learning-related process when the driver is not permitted to stop the learning-related process.

In the fifth embodiment, the control routine of the disaster information transmission processing of fig. 5 is executed as in the first embodiment, and the control routine of the learning stop processing shown in fig. 14 is executed. Fig. 14 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning stop process in the fifth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU40 of the vehicle 3 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S701, the output device control unit 53 determines whether disaster information is received from the server 2. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received from the server 2, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received from the server 2, the present control routine proceeds to step S702.

In step S702, the output device control section 53 confirms the permission to stop the learning-related process to the driver of the vehicle 3 via the HMI 31. For example, the output device control unit 53 confirms the permission to the driver by text or sound via the HMI 31.

Next, in step S703, the learning unit 51 determines whether or not the driver allows the learning-related process to stop, based on the input of the driver to the HMI 31. If it is determined that the driver does not permit the stop of the learning-related process, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the driver permits the stop of the learning-related process, the present control routine proceeds to step S704.

In step S704, the learning unit 51 stops the learning-related process as in step S202 of fig. 6. After step S704, the present control routine ends. In this case, the learning unit 51 restarts the learning-related process, for example, when a predetermined time elapses, when the vehicle 3 restarts, when the driver of the vehicle 3 instructs the restart of the learning-related process via the HMI31, or when the server 2 instructs the restart of the learning-related process. In addition, the control routine of fig. 14 may be modified in the same manner as the control routine of fig. 6.

< Sixth embodiment >

The configuration and control of the machine learning device according to the sixth embodiment are basically the same as those of the machine learning device according to the third embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a sixth embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly in a part different from the third embodiment.

As described above, in the third embodiment, in the vehicle in the disaster area, the amount of power consumption in the learning-related process is reduced. On the other hand, even if the vehicle is not located in the disaster area when the disaster occurs, the destination of the vehicle may be the disaster area. In this case, it is considered that electric power is supplied from the vehicle to the outside after reaching the disaster-stricken area. Therefore, in the sixth embodiment, when the supply of electric power from the vehicle 3 to the outside is predicted based on the disaster information and the destination of the vehicle 3, the learning unit 51 reduces the amount of electric power consumption in the learning-related process, as compared with the case where the supply of electric power is not predicted. This makes it possible to suppress power consumption in a suitable vehicle in consideration of the destination.

The destination of the vehicle 3 is input by the driver of the vehicle 3, and is stored in the navigation system 34 or the like, for example. The position information acquisition unit 52 acquires the stored destination of the vehicle 3. The destination of the vehicle 3 is periodically transmitted from the vehicle 3 to the server 2 together with identification information (e.g., identification number) of the vehicle 3, and stored in the storage device 22 of the server 2.

In the sixth embodiment, the control routine of the vehicle determination process shown in fig. 15 is executed, and the control routine of the learning stop process of fig. 11 is executed as in the third embodiment. Fig. 15 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the vehicle determination process in the sixth embodiment of the invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 24 of the server 2 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S801, the processor 24 determines whether disaster information is received. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S802.

In step S802, the processor 24 determines a vehicle to be a disaster area by comparing the location information of the disaster area included in the disaster information with the destinations of the vehicles stored for each vehicle.

Next, in step S803, the processor 24 transmits a stop instruction of the learning-related process to the vehicle determined in step S802. After step S803, the present control routine ends.

In addition, disaster information may be input to the server 2 by an operator of the server 2 or the like, and the processor 24 may determine whether or not disaster information is input to the server 2 in step S801. In step S803, the processor 24 may transmit a power suppression instruction to the vehicle destined for the disaster area instead of the learning stop instruction. The present location and destination of the vehicle may be periodically transmitted to the server 2, and the processor 24 may transmit a stop instruction or a power suppression instruction of the learning-related process to the vehicle in the disaster area and the vehicle at the disaster area.

< Seventh embodiment >

The structure and control of the machine learning device of the seventh embodiment are basically the same as those of the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, a seventh embodiment of the present invention will be described below focusing on a portion different from the first embodiment.

In the seventh embodiment, the learning of the neural network model is performed in the server 2 instead of the ECU40 of the vehicle 3. That is, the server 2 functions as a machine learning device.

A training data set for learning of the neural network model is created in the plurality of vehicles and transmitted from the plurality of vehicles to the server 2. The processor 24 of the server 2 performs learning of the neural network model using a large number of training data sets and transmits the learned neural network model to the vehicle via the communication interface 21. At this time, in the vehicle 3, power is consumed when the learned neural network model is received and stored from the server 2.

Therefore, when disaster information is acquired, the processor 24 of the server 2 stops the transmission of the learned neural network model to the vehicle 3. In this way, in the vehicle 3, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the amount of electricity that can be supplied from the vehicle 3 to the outside at the time of a disaster.

Fig. 16 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the model transmission stop process in the seventh embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 24 of the server 2 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S901, the processor 24 determines whether disaster information is received. When it is determined that disaster information has not been received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that disaster information is received, the present control routine advances to step S902.

In step S902, the processor 24 stops transmission of the learned neural network model to the vehicle 3. After step S902, the present control routine ends. In this case, the processor 24 resumes the transmission of the learned neural network model, for example, when a predetermined time has elapsed or when a disaster has been eliminated.

In addition, disaster information may be input to the server 2 by an operator of the server 2 or the like, and the processor 24 may determine whether or not disaster information is input to the server 2 in step S901.

In addition, step S402 of fig. 10 may be executed between steps S901 and S902, and in step S902, the processor 24 may stop transmission of the learned neural network model to the vehicle determined in step S402. Similarly, step S802 of fig. 15 may be executed between steps S901 and S902, and in step S902, the processor 24 may stop transmission of the learned neural network model to the vehicle determined in step S802.

In the seventh embodiment, as in the above-described embodiment, control for stopping the learning-related process in the vehicle 3 or control for reducing the amount of power consumption of the learning-related process in the vehicle 3 may be performed. In this case, the learning unit 51 stops creation of the training data set and transmission of the training data set to the server 2 when stopping the learning-related process, and reduces the frequency of generating the training data set or the frequency of transmitting the training data set to the server 2 when reducing the power consumption of the learning-related process.
